originalContract.androidStorage: CacheManager userInfo_<getKey()> stores AES ciphertext. get/put derive the key from AppConst.androidId UTF-8 bytes [0,16); put returns false on encryption/storage exceptions; get catches and returns null on failures.
originalContract.iosStorageMapping: Same existing LoginManager userInfo_<sourceURL> account in KeychainHelper.loginService, AfterFirstUnlock protection and existing system Keychain encryption. No Android-ID/AES key is fabricated, stored in generic variables or exported. This preserves plaintext API values but does not expose an Android AES ciphertext mirror through cache.get(userInfo_...).

production: BookSource raw nullable String/Boolean/Unit delegate only to ProductionRulePlatform, using the same RuntimeTask, HTTP/Rhino environment, explicit stateOwner/source URL and original deadline.

Dedicated source.login-info operation on existing LegadoPersistentStateHost validates exact source bytes/current revision. It never grants generic cache keys, chooses a path or instantiates another store/VM/network stack.

AppLegadoOwnedStateBacking delegates to the same injected LoginManager and same credential storage. Existing form Map writes are visible as raw JSON; raw JSON writes remain visible to the existing form parser; arbitrary non-JSON and empty Strings remain byte-exact.

Strict Keychain reads distinguish missing from locked/malformed/read failure. Known rejected put writes return false; failed remove throws STATE_IO. Unchanged values do not write or advance revision. Same-item writes retain original immediate last-writer-wins behavior; no CAS or atomic multi-owner transaction is invented.

Legacy UserDefaults credentials migrate through one shared insert-only Keychain core used by both runtime raw and existing Map reads. Present non-JSON/empty values never authorize migration. A failed insert rereads the winner; accepted insert returns the identical logical credential without another read. Migration changes protection/storage only and adds no synchronous revision-queue work to existing forms.

Checks and callback effect-seal claim precede noninterruptible mutation. Accepted writes advance existing loginInfoRevision and notification. MayCommit/Committed receipts survive a late native cancellation; later JS statements do not execute. Source revoke and already-cancelled tasks reject before owner access.
Credential I/O executes off main with SourcePerfTrace and counts only; source URLs, raw values and arbitrary storage error descriptions are excluded from new diagnostics.

limits: Actual Swift SDK/Keychain/JNI executions remain zero for these changed inputs. Native fixtures are definitions, not passing evidence. Windows peer stores only synthetic credentials and does not establish secure native persistence.

iOS deliberately fails closed with typed STATE_IO on locked/unreadable credentials instead of converting operational failures to original Android getLoginInfo null. Put false denotes a known rejected native write; cancellation/unknown effects remain typed.
Raw credential values are bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes and request JSON to524288 bytes at this native boundary; Android does not define this native transport ceiling.

getLoginInfoMap dynamic/static loginUi defaults, loginUrl/login/loginAction, browser/WebJS and the rest of source Java host ABI remain unfinished; this raw credential binding is not complete login UI compatibility.
No raw user logs, private bookSource.json or actual credentials were read. No canonical/Git/cloud mutation was performed by this stage.
